topics.title: Single-host observability
topics.summary: Inspect current Linux host and agent observations from the local collector without connecting to a receiver.

scenarios.expected: The JSON envelope identifies the metrics domain and reports rows within the lookback window, subject to local retention.

proofs.scope: The extracted watermark helper is monotone and preserves the committed value when the caller reports a failed flush.
proofs.assumptions: The caller supplies a truthful flush result. Filesystem durability and the daemon's observation of flush outcomes require runtime evidence.

proofs.scope: The independent natural-number watermark model is monotone over a trace of candidate flushes.
proofs.assumptions: The model takes abstract flush outcomes as inputs and does not model Parquet publication.

topics.title: Spindle and canonical custody
topics.summary: Inspect durable local Spindle and optional receiver custody. Each contiguous receiver frontier belongs to one configured origin.

scenarios.description: Compare the Spindle, receiver, and collector frontiers
scenarios.expected: The response reports which stores can be reached and their known progress. A custody acknowledgment does not establish query visibility.

proofs.scope: Publication in the independent custody model requires successful full byte readback.
proofs.assumptions: The model uses abstract storage and message operations. Receiver durability and actual retry behavior require integration tests.

topics.title: Distributed observability
topics.summary: Follow multiple Spindle origins forwarding to one authenticated canonical receiver and compare their separate progress.

scenarios.description: Inspect known origin frontiers at the configured authority
scenarios.expected: The receiver returns its authority and a prefix per authorized origin. Configure FABRIC_ENDPOINT and FABRIC_CREDENTIAL_FILE first.

proofs.scope: The independent custody model preserves a contiguous source prefix over arbitrary modeled event traces.
proofs.assumptions: The result covers modeled events. It does not establish deployment availability or bound network delay.

topics.title: Source-fenced receiver queries
topics.summary: Use the typed receiver API for source-scoped queries with a bounded snapshot, budget, and coverage report.

scenarios.description: Read original evidence for a known authorized canonical record
scenarios.expected: A configured receiver returns the original JSON for an authorized record or an explicit error.

topics.title: Receipt projection readiness
topics.summary: Check whether the exact observation in a local Spindle receipt is queryable at the selected projection target.

scenarios.description: Wait for a locally committed row
scenarios.expected: The command returns visible only for exact committed evidence, pending at a lagging frontier, or unavailable when evidence cannot be established.
The receiver reports distinct custody and projection frontiers when it can establish the scope and the requested receipt.

proofs.scope: The frontier decision advances only through a contiguous, origin-qualified completed range.
proofs.assumptions: The caller supplies authenticated origin and completed publication evidence. Transport, Parquet and redb durability require runtime checks.

topics.title: Effective settings and headroom
topics.summary: Inspect versioned settings, overrides, and the Linux limit behind the automatic hot ring budget.

scenarios.expected: The report gives resolved fields, each value’s source, and the inputs used for the automatic hot ring budget.

proofs.scope: The extracted implementation reserves a quarter of a known capacity, rounded up.
proofs.assumptions: The caller supplies an accurate finite capacity. Linux limit discovery and memory behavior require runtime checks.

proofs.scope: The extracted implementation returns idle capacity while preserving live charges.
proofs.assumptions: The caller accounts for ownership, including work still in flight, and applies the decision only to an elastic resource.
